messages:
maria_support: customer reports intermittent SSE disconnects + partial final chunks when behind an NLB -> client reconnect loop. Happens after ~6m of idle streaming. They see a 200 and then the stream stops mid-chunk, client reconnects and gets duplicated prefix.

sarah_support: asking for repro steps/logs. did they share request headers or a curl command? :thinking_face:

maria_support: pasted curl they used in the ticket and a tcpdump excerpt:
```
curl -v -N \ 
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer <redacted>\" \ 
  -H \"Accept: text/event-stream\" \ 
  https://api.redwood.example/v1/stream?model=redwood-lite
```
Response stream arrives for minutes then stops. tcpdump shows server FIN then NLB sending RST ~1s later. hex shows chunk boundary cut: `...\n0\r\n` becomes `0\r` then connection close.

maria_support: customer is on our Dedicated NLB + nginx ingress (k8s). They said they don't see nginx logs for the final write.

jon_eng_sre: quick hypothesis: two separate things colliding -> NLB idle/connection-drain behavior + proxy buffering or proxy_protocol mismatch. If NLB drops at idle it can send RST if backend already closed. That can cause truncated chunk seen by client. Also check whether nginx has `proxy_buffering on` or is aggregating chunked responses.

lin_eng_runtime: checked runtime logs for that customer id, we see final write (chunk terminator) and then close socket with FIN. Kernel send queue drained. No error on our side. But packet capture at edge shows RST from NLB shortly after FIN. suggests NLB connection-drain/idle timer is racing with the client.

jon_eng_sre: repro checklist for support to run with customer (short commands):
- curl using `--no-buffer -N` from client side to reproduce
- capture `tcpdump -i any host <customer-ip> and port 443` on their side and on our edge if possible
- get nginx ingress config (proxy_http_version, proxy_buffering, proxy_request_buffering)

sarah_support: added this checklist to the ticket and customer will run tonight. any immediate mitigations we can recommend?

lin_eng_runtime: quick mitigations:
- ensure nginx ingress has `proxy_http_version 1.1; proxy_set_header Connection \"\"; proxy_buffering off; chunked_transfer_encoding on;` so it streams raw chunks and doesn't buffer/truncate.
- set NLB idle timeout higher (default 350s) or enable application-level keepalive heartbeats from client after ~60s so the NLB doesn't consider connection idle.
- for ALB/Cloudflare users note Cloudflare 100s idle can also cut streams; recommend shorter app heartbeats or Cloudflare Stream rules.

jon_eng_sre: also ask infra to check for `proxy_protocol` enabled mismatch between NLB and nginx; if proxy_protocol v2 is expected but absent, NGINX could mis-parse leading bytes and treat stream weirdly. Not common but seen in similar incidents.

maria_support: customer says they use our JS SDK which auto-reconnects every 5s, so they see duplicate prefixes. They prefer server to send an explicit final event rather than abrupt truncation.

jon_eng_sre: long-term fix: make runtime emit a small keepalive comment/event every 30s for long polling streams. Short-term: we can tag the request with `X-Redwood-Stream-Heartbeat: 30` and runtime will send a \":heartbeat:\" event if present (we recently added this flag to staging).

deploy-bot: rollout: ingress nginx config tweak (proxy_buffering off + http1.1) deployed to staging at 2412349000, will promote to canary tomorrow.

ops-bot: linked ticket #SUP-21345 and incident tracker.

sarah_support: customer ran tcpdump and confirmed RST from NLB following our FIN. They will try SDK heartbeat patch tonight and confirm. I'll follow up after their test. :thumbsup:

maria_support: thanks — next steps: 1) customer tests heartbeat-enabled SDK; 2) we push ingress canary tweak if customer still sees truncation; 3) if persists, collect full pcap across edge and backend and open a networking postmortem.

jon_eng_sre: one more note: when debugging, use `curl --no-buffer -N` AND `openssl s_client -quiet -connect api.redwood.example:443` to observe raw TCP behavior. RST vs FIN makes the root cause clear.

lin_eng_runtime: I'll add server-side logging to emit a final marker `X-STREAM-FINISHED` in the last chunk so we can tell the difference between server-closed vs network-truncated in traces.

maria_support: updated ticket with plan. closing thread here until customer confirms.
